title: Auctions with LLM Summaries

problem.claim: The paper studies auctions in which bidders compete for placement of content within an LLM-generated summary.

gap.claim: Classic ad auction settings such as position auctions do not directly handle general LLM-generated display formats.

contributions.claim: A factorized framework coordinates an auction module and an LLM module through a prediction model to produce welfare-maximizing summaries in an incentive-compatible manner.
The paper provides a theoretical analysis of the proposed framework.
Synthetic experiments evaluate the feasibility, validity, and welfare comparisons of the system.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their factorized framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical analysis and synthetic experiments concerning feasibility, validity, and welfare comparisons.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper introduces auctions for content placement within LLM-generated summaries.
The setting extends classic ad auction formats to general LLM-generated displays.
The authors propose a factorized auction-and-LLM framework mediated by a prediction model.
The paper reports theoretical analysis and synthetic experiments assessing feasibility, validity, and welfare comparisons.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines auction and LLM modules through a prediction model while targeting incentive compatibility and welfare maximization.

interpretation.claim: Separating market allocation from content generation may make complex display formats more tractable to model.

application.claim: Use modular interfaces between allocation mechanisms and generative systems when designing auctions for variable-format content.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the modular framework achieves its welfare or incentive-compatibility properties.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the auction mechanism, prediction model, or LLM implementation.
The abstract does not report theoretical assumptions, experimental settings, quantitative results, or welfare comparison outcomes.
